name: spiny-back-beetle
status: walking loop study; not installed in runtime
artworkMethod: one full horizontal strip of redrawn walking cels; no part transforms or synthetic motion interpolation

normalization.calibration: one common scale using rigid upper-carapace width; register body apex while feet move

prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Actual production 2D GAME WALK-CYCLE animation artwork. Edit image1, the approved seed on a six-slot transparent canvas, into ONE COMPLETE SIX-CEL HORIZONTAL WALK STRIP in one generation. Output ONE WIDE transparent RGBA image, exactly six equal slots in a single row, ideally 3072x512. Image2 is the APPROVED neutral character and scale/style authority. The existing neutral legs in image1 may be redrawn into a walk stride in slot1; preserve the body. Same character, facing lower-left, three-quarter front-left view, same burgundy carapace with thin dark teal contours, EXACTLY THREE large ivory dorsal spikes, two inward-curving ivory pincers, amber eyes, six short articulated burgundy legs with dark pointed feet. Smooth detailed painted rendering matching image2, NOT pixel art. The same single beetle appears in all six slots with EXACTLY THE SAME RIGID CARAPACE SCALE, SHAPE, DETAILS, POSITION, LIGHTING and largest-spike tip coordinates. Keep head, face, eyes and pincers at the identical relaxed pose across all six cels. No growing/shrinking, no body rocking, no squash, no jumping, no attacking, no blinking, no whole-image transform wobble. Only legs and their joints perform the gait. Body stays in place because the game engine supplies world movement.

Create a clearly readable grounded SIX-LEGGED ALTERNATING TRIPOD gait: on the visible near side the FRONT and REAR leg move together while the MIDDLE leg does the opposite; the far-side legs are out of phase with the near side. At least three feet support the body at all times. Supporting feet remain low and push back; swinging feet visibly lift by only 12-20px through bent joints then reach forward toward lower-left. Preserve short sturdy leg lengths and original anatomy, no additional legs. This is newly drawn cel animation, not a repeated flat sprite with feet shifted as a single block. Keep overlapping far-side legs correctly behind the abdomen; near-side legs in front. All feet/spikes must fit inside each slot with ample transparent margins.

Six loop poses, evenly progressing through one entire gait cycle. CEL1, A contact: near FRONT+REAR feet reach forward toward lower-left and touch the ground; near MIDDLE foot is behind, about to swing. Far legs opposite. CEL2, A support/pass: near front+rear feet push back on ground, near middle knee flexes and its foot lifts and passes forward; far legs opposite. CEL3, transfer to B: near middle foot extends forward to land, near front+rear knees start lifting feet from their rear stance, far legs opposite. CEL4, B contact: near MIDDLE foot planted forward, near front+rear feet behind preparing to swing, opposite of CEL1. CEL5, B support/pass: near middle foot pushes back on ground while near front+rear knees flex and lift feet together to pass forward, far legs opposite. CEL6, transfer back to A: near front+rear feet reach forward to land, near middle begins lifting from rear stance. CEL6 must naturally continue into CEL1 with NO idle/rest pose and NO duplicated start cel. These are six DIFFERENT leg poses forming a seamless looping walk. Rigid beetle body at the same coordinates and scale in every cel, clear leg alternation, measured short strides, understated motion.

Transparent background only, no floor, shadows, scene, labels, numbers, text, borders, targets, trails, smear duplicates, particles, gore, blur, checkerboard or watermark. Exactly SIX full-body cels in one horizontal row, no extra rows and no cut-off appendages.
